messages.subject: P-Value for pegas amova
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am using poppr to run an amova using the pegas method  and everything runs fine, but it does not output any p-values. Is there a way to calculate the p-value, like with the ade4 method?

Pegas outputs a p-value when run on its own, but it cannot handle missing data in the distance matrix, which is why i'm running it through poppr, and also why i'm confused that there is no p-value.

Thank you for any help you can provide.

-Kris

messages.subject: Re: [poppr] P-Value for pegas amova
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Unlike ade4, pegas runs the permutations within the amova function, so you want to use the `nperm` parameter to set the number of permutations. See the documentation: https://grunwaldlab.github.io/poppr/reference/poppr.amova.html

Hope that helps,

Zhian

messages.subject: MLG accumulation curve
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I was wondering if it is feasible to estimate the total number of MLGs in a population based on a subsample of that population? i.e. if we were able to increase the number of samples, how many more MLGs might we expect to find?

One possible way I thought this might be achieved is an MLG accumulation curve, akin to a species accumulation curve. I understand there is an MLG accumulation curve based on the number of loci, but I thought it might be more appropriate to use the number of samples instead.

I have attached an example script of my attempt using the Pinf dataset and the farthest algorithm to define the threshold for clonal lineages.

It follows the following steps:
Identify a distance threshold for MLGs using farthest algorithm
For varying number of samples (from 10 to 80 by 10) the script will:
get 10 replicate subsamples of samples size x
count the number of MLGs for each subsample
return a data table like the following, where sample sizes are along the top and the rows show the number of mlgs for each repeat.
          10 20 30 40 50 60 70 80
repeat_1   9 13 21 26 30 36 40 45
repeat_2   8 16 23 27 29 35 43 47
repeat_3   8 14 20 24 30 38 39 44
repeat_4   8 15 21 27 35 38 38 46
repeat_5   9 13 20 29 33 41 40 45
repeat_6   9 12 21 26 35 37 44 46
repeat_7   8 15 19 27 30 37 39 45
repeat_8   9 18 25 29 34 33 41 47
repeat_9   9 16 18 29 33 38 43 46
repeat_10  8 16 22 23 36 34 40 45

Using this data we can plot a trendline and potentially make predictions about the number of overall MLG.

I realise that there is lots of potential for error with this, but if anyone has comments or suggestions please do let me know.

Thanks again providing the package and support!

Best wishes
Ollie
